# Security

Baseline security applies whatever the chosen authentication mode.

Marker after the identifier: a tool name = tooled constraint (the build or the commit fails); `guidance` = rule of conduct checked in review.

## Base rules

### Rules

- **CORE-030** · `gitleaks` — Secrets and environment-specific values come from environment variables read by a `pydantic-settings` class; `.env.example` is committed and `.env` is ignored.
  Why: Configuration that differs per environment must never be a code change, and a typed settings class fails at startup rather than at the first request.
- **CORE-031** · `gitleaks` — No credential, token or private key is ever committed; the gitleaks pre-commit hook blocks the commit.
  Why: A secret in history is compromised even after it is removed.
- **CORE-032** · guidance — The only diagnostic endpoint exposed is `/health`; no endpoint returns configuration, environment or dumps.
  Why: A diagnostics endpoint is a configuration leak waiting for the first scan.
- **CORE-033** · guidance — CORS origins are an explicit list read from settings; `allow_origins=["*"]` is never used outside local development.
  Why: A wildcard origin turns every browser into a client of the API.
- **CORE-034** · guidance — The response security headers set by the middleware (`X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options`, HSTS) are never removed without an ADR.
  Why: Starlette sets none of them by default; the skeleton adds them and each one closes a class of browser attacks for free.
- **CORE-035** · `pip-audit` — A dependency carrying a known vulnerability fails the pipeline, `pip-audit` running on the resolved lockfile.
  Why: Most breaches exploit a known, already patched vulnerability.
- **CORE-036** · `pytest` — The interactive documentation and the OpenAPI schema are served only when `APP_ENV` is not `production`.
  Why: `/docs` publishes every route, every schema and every field name to anyone who asks.
- **CORE-037** · `pytest` — The 500 handler answers a problem document without the traceback; the traceback goes to the logs only.
  Why: A traceback hands an attacker the library versions and the internal file layout.

### Anti-patterns

- **CORE-AP-030** · `gitleaks` — A password or API key written as a default value in the settings class.
  Why: The value is committed, shared and impossible to rotate per environment.
  Instead: A field without a default, documented in `.env.example`, so a missing value fails at startup.
- **CORE-AP-031** · guidance — `FastAPI(debug=True)` left on outside local development to "help debugging in staging".
  Why: Staging is reachable and the debug response prints the exception and the source.
  Instead: Read the logs, which carry the same information without publishing it.
- **CORE-AP-032** · guidance — `allow_origins=["*"]` with `allow_credentials=True` to make a local front end work.
  Why: The shortcut ships to production because nobody remembers it, and the browser sends the cookies with it.
  Instead: The local origin in the development settings and the real one in production.

### Expected environment variables

| Variable | Example | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `SESSION_SECRET` | `` | Signing key of the session cookie; generate one per environment and never commit it (SECS-002). |
| `SESSION_COOKIE_NAME` | `app_session` | Cookie name; a name of its own avoids colliding with another application on the same domain. |

## Option `security-session`

Cookie session held by the API itself, for a front end served from the same site.

### Rules

- **SECS-001** · `pytest` — The session cookie is `HttpOnly`, `Secure` and `SameSite=Lax`, and its name is not the framework default.
  Why: `HttpOnly` keeps it out of JavaScript, `Secure` off plaintext, `SameSite` off cross-site requests.
- **SECS-002** · `pytest` — The signing secret comes from the environment and has no default value; the application refuses to start without it.
  Why: A default secret is a public secret, and it signs every session of every deployment that forgot to set it.
- **SECS-003** · guidance — Passwords are stored hashed with Argon2 through `passlib`; no reversible encryption, no unsalted hash.
  Why: A leaked database must not be a leaked password list.
- **SECS-004** · `pytest` — Login and logout rotate the session identifier.
  Why: Without rotation, a session fixed before login stays valid after it.
- **SECS-005** · `pytest` — A route that requires authentication declares it through the shared dependency; no route reads the session itself.
  Why: A per-route check is a per-route bug, and the OpenAPI document stops describing what is protected.

### Anti-patterns

- **SECS-AP-001** · guidance — Storing the user identifier in an unsigned cookie read directly by the routes.
  Why: The client edits the cookie and becomes whoever it wants.
  Instead: The signed session cookie, whose content the client cannot forge.
- **SECS-AP-002** · guidance — Disabling `Secure` on the cookie so that local HTTP development works.
  Why: The setting ships to production, where the cookie then travels in plaintext.
  Instead: Serve local development over HTTPS, or read the flag from the settings.
